content.text: PROPOSAL FOR HIV/AIDS AND COVID-19 AWARENESS PROGRAMME FOR DESIGN AND BUILD FOR MODERNIZATION OF THE MALINDI WHARF AREA AT DAR ES SALAAM PORT.

The Government of Tanzania, through the Tanzania Ports Authority (TPA), is upgrading the Malindi Wharf at the Port of Dar es Salaam to enhance cargo handling capacity and operational efficiency. As the country's main seaport and a key regional trade gateway for several landlocked countries, the port plays a significant role in East Africa's economy. The project includes construction of a multipurpose berth and supporting infrastructure such as access roads, operational yards, utilities, and improved port systems, under a Design and Build contract led by China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd.

Large construction projects pose public health risks, particularly the spread of HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 due to workforce mobility and limited access to health services. Given Tanzania's HIV burden, targeted workplace  interventions  are  essential  to  protect  workers,  surrounding  communities,  and  overall productivity.

In response to these challenges, Vision Care Clinic proposes to implement a comprehensive HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 awareness and prevention programme tailored specifically for personnel engaged in the Malindi Wharf modernization project. The programme will focus on enhancing awareness, promoting safe  practices,  facilitating  access  to  testing  and  counselling  services,  and  strengthening  linkages  to treatment and care.

The programme also fulfills legal and contractual requirements under national laws and international standards,  while  ensuring  strict  confidentiality  of  health  information  in  line  with  the  HIV  and  AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act.

Globally,  about  40.8  million  people  were  living  with  HIV  by  2024,  with  Tanzania  accounting  for approximately  1.6  million  cases  and  a  national  prevalence  of  4.4%.  Although  new  infections  have declined,  HIV  transmission  remains  influenced  by  factors  such  as  demographic  differences,  socioeconomic conditions, and high-risk groups including mobile populations like construction workers.

Construction  settings  increase  vulnerability  to  HIV  and  COVID-19  due  to  worker  mobility,  social interaction,  and  separation  from  families.  Workplace  awareness  programs  are  therefore  essential  to reduce transmission, promote safe behaviors, encourage voluntary testing, and minimize stigma, while also  maintaining  productivity  and  reducing  workforce  turnover.  These  interventions  contribute  to national efforts aimed at lowering new infections and improving community health outcomes.

The Malindi Wharf modernization project, implemented by the Tanzania Ports Authority on behalf of the Government  of  Tanzania,  is  being  executed  by  China  Harbour  Engineering  Company  Ltd  under  a Design and Build contract. The project includes development of a multipurpose berth and supporting infrastructure  such  as  yards,  roads,  utilities,  and  drainage  systems,  all  aimed  at  improving  port efficiency and strengthening its role as a key regional trade hub.

In response, Vision Care Clinic proposes a targeted HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention program for project workers, focusing on education, risk reduction, testing, and linkage to care services to support a healthier and safer working environment.

Vision  and  Care  Clinic  proposes  a  comprehensive  HIV/AIDS  Awareness  and  Prevention  Training Program  for  employees  working  in  the  construction  industry.  Construction  workers  often  work  in environments that expose them to higher health risks due to mobility, long working hours, and limited access to health education.
This program aims to improve awareness, encourage safe behaviors, promote HIV testing, and reduce stigma within the workplace.
The following are the objectives of the HIV/AIDS and COVID 19 awareness program:
 Increase Knowledge about HIV/AID and Capacity Building for Preventive measures.
 Promote Safe Behaviors and Risk Reduction
 Strengthen Access to Prevention and Health Services
 Integrate Health and Safety into Workplace Operations
 Reduce Stigma, Discrimination, and Improve Workplace Welfare
 Enhance Monitoring, Evaluation, and Continuous Improvement
The training will use participatory and interactive learning approaches including:
 Guidance on Voluntary Counselling and Testing (VCT)
The following is the plan for the six month awareness program concerning HIV/AIDS and COVID 19 issues in the Malindi Wharf modernization project.
 Basic understanding of HIV and AIDS  Hold introductory sensitization meeting on HIV/AIDS and prevention measures

 Organize HIV/AIDS awareness training sessions for workers and staff  Train peer educators on basic counseling and prevention messaging  Distribute IEC materials (posters, brochures) on HIV prevention
 Conduct behavior change communication (BCC) sessions on safe practices  Organize condom education and correct-use demonstrations  Facilitate peer-to-peer discussions on risk reduction strategies

 Arrange voluntary counseling and testing (VCT) campaign at the workplace  Link workers to nearby health facilities for HIV services and support  Conduct referral system awareness sessions for treatment and care

 Integrate HIV/AIDS and occupational health topics into toolbox talks  Conduct anti-stigma and discrimination awareness campaign  Organize workplace dialogue sessions on employee welfare and inclusion
 Conduct end line survey to measure knowledge and behavior change  Review program achievements against baseline results  Hold feedback and lessons learned workshop for improvement planning
Vision and Care Clinic will provide:
 Qualified health educators for conducting training
 Monthly training sessions to the community members and workers
 Training materials and handouts such as magazines and notices.
 HIV/AIDS awareness posters for the workplace
 Monitoring and evaluation of the program
By the end of the training program:
 To enhance understanding of HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 transmission, prevention, and control through structured training, awareness campaigns, and peer education.
 To encourage positive behavioral change among workers that reduces exposure to infection and promotes safe practices in both workplace and community settings.
 To  improve  access  to  voluntary  counselling  and  testing  (VCT),  treatment  services,  and preventive materials such as condoms and personal protective equipment.
 To incorporate HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 preventive measures into daily construction activities, site safety systems, and project management procedures.
 To promote a supportive working environment by reducing stigma, encouraging inclusion, and safeguarding the dignity of affected workers.
 To track implementation effectiveness, evaluate outcomes, and continuously improve program delivery based on feedback and data.

Vision  Care  Clinic  is  committed  to  improving  community  health  through  education,  prevention,  and support  services.  This  HIV/AIDS  awareness  program  will  help  create  a  safer,  healthier,  and  more informed workplace for construction company employees.
We look forward to working together to promote health and wellbeing in the workplace.
